title: Why are so many brands ditching celebrities for ordinary people?
tldr: Explores the shift away from A-list celebrity endorsements toward everyday, relatable people in advertising. Directly speaks to the human-centered, people-over-polish content trend.
why_fresh: emerging casting trend away from celebrities
angle: Write about why relatability now outperforms fame — and what it means for brand storytelling built around real people.

title: The AI backlash is getting louder. Brands should pay attention.
tldr: Consumer frustration with AI is becoming a trust and reputation issue, with campaigns like Polaroid's leaning into anti-AI, human sentiment. Vital for comms leaders navigating brand positioning.
angle: How brands can turn the AI backlash into a human-first positioning advantage.

title: The real reasons employees leave
tldr: Employees leave because they don't feel connected, not because of communication volume — reframing internal comms around belonging. Strong internal comms/EGC angle.
angle: Connection over cadence: rethinking internal communications as belonging-building, not message delivery.

title: I Am Begging Websites To Remember They Are Read By Human Beings
tldr: A pointed rant against dehumanized, SEO-bloated web content and a plea for content that respects reader dignity. Captures the human-over-polish zeitgeist sharply.
angle: Reclaiming dignity in web writing: why human-first content is now a competitive edge, not a nicety.

title: The myth of the changing consumer
tldr: Argues that consumers aren't fundamentally changing — you need context behind the trend before reacting. A useful corrective for strategists chasing every media-consumption headline.
angle: Stop chasing 'consumer change': how to read context before rebuilding your content strategy.

title: Media Briefing: The post-traffic era of the open web is taking shape
tldr: Publishers are trading search-driven scale for stronger brands and diversified audiences as referral traffic collapses. Core shift for anyone building owned media.
angle: Building for the post-traffic web: why brand and direct audience relationships now beat search scale.

title: The case for and against the 'programmatic-ification' of the creator economy
tldr: Creator marketing is racing toward AI-driven ad-stack automation, risking turning creator trust into commoditized inventory. A sharp tension for the creator economy's future.
angle: When creator trust becomes ad inventory: the cost of automating the human out of influence.

title: Can we gamify that? Innovators turning investigations into video games
tldr: Newsrooms are transforming investigations on spying scandals and vote rigging into interactive video games. A genuinely novel storytelling format.
angle: Playable journalism: what gamified investigations teach content teams about narrative transportation.

title: How Dr Pepper's 'Fansville' campaign stays relevant and drives outcomes
tldr: A concrete breakdown of how a nine-season college-football campaign uses personalization to keep lifting sales. A rare longevity-plus-outcomes campaign case study.
why_fresh: ongoing campaign, but useful case study
angle: How to sustain a long-running campaign world without audience fatigue.

title: Claude is changing how it generates prose to be more detectable (and maybe worse?)
tldr: Anthropic is tweaking Claude's writing to be more identifiable as AI, raising questions about prose quality and detectability. Relevant to anyone using LLMs for content.
angle: When AI is deliberately made to sound like AI: implications for content teams relying on LLM prose.

title: OpenAI Business CMO Colin Fleming Says Everyone Can Do Marketing Now. So Who Gets to Say No?
tldr: As AI democratizes marketing production, the question becomes who holds editorial judgment and governance. A pointed take on content governance in the AI era.
why_fresh: fresh governance angle on AI democratization
angle: When everyone can make content, taste and the power to say 'no' become the scarce skill.

title: How Athleta is revamping its brand narrative with bolder purpose
tldr: Athleta is rebuilding its corporate narrative around a bolder brand purpose. A useful, concrete brand-narrative case study.
angle: What makes a purpose-led narrative land vs. feel hollow.

title: The three-question framework that transforms commodity content into high-value thought leadership
tldr: A simple three-question framework for elevating generic content into genuine thought leadership. Practical craft tool for strategists.
angle: A repeatable filter for turning commodity content into thought leadership worth reading.

title: Daily social media use beyond 2.5 hours tracks with depression, analysis finds
tldr: New analysis links heavy daily social media use with depression, informing how we think about audience media-consumption habits and platform design ethics.
angle: What the 2.5-hour threshold means for brands whose content lives inside the harm.

title: RuPay, tgthr. Originals bring brand storytelling to microdrama with 'Sarva Groom Sampanna'
tldr: A brand is using the booming microdrama format for storytelling — an emerging short-form vertical worth watching. Concrete branded-content example.
angle: Microdramas as brand storytelling: the next short-form frontier beyond Reels and Shorts.
